methodological_rigor.justification: The study combines a single-center retrospective cohort (n=277) with PSM and a network meta-analysis of only 4 RCTs. PSM used a narrow covariate set (age, brain metastases, pleural/pericardial effusion, chemotherapy regimen) and did not include PD-L1 status or performance status, which the authors acknowledge is a limitation (Section 4). No a priori power calculation is reported, and the post-PSM arms (80 vs 80) are modest for detecting OS differences. Subgroup analyses are explicitly exploratory with no multiplicity correction (acknowledged in limitations), and the NMA relies on fixed-effects pooling with just four trials and indirect comparisons, limiting inference. Statistical methods are generally standard (Kaplan–Meier, log-rank, Cox models, Mantel–Haenszel, inverse variance, node-splitting), but no handling of missing PD-L1 data (45.8% missing) beyond complete-case subgroup analysis is described.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is a hybrid: a retrospective single-center cohort (2b/4) combined with a network meta-analysis of four RCTs. The highest supported LoE from the NMA component maps to 2a given it synthesizes RCTs but is primarily an indirect comparison with a small evidence base and known limitations. Clinically, the question is relevant for a common oncology scenario (first-line EGFR/ALK-wild-type non-squamous NSCLC), with patient-relevant endpoints (PFS, OS, AEs). However, the main conclusion is cautionary—no clear subgroup where benefit outweighs toxicity—so the findings reinforce the status quo (I+C) rather than practice-changing, limiting translational impact to risk–benefit discussion.

reporting_quality.justification: Because of the hybrid design, both STROBE (retrospective cohort) and PRISMA-NMA apply; the authors explicitly cite PRISMA-NMA adherence with checklist in File S2 and provide a flow diagram, risk-of-bias assessment, and search strategy, which are strengths. For the cohort portion, inclusion/exclusion criteria, PSM procedure, and endpoint definitions (RECIST 1.1, CTCAE v5.0) are reported, but formal STROBE adherence is not stated and there is no explicit mention of protocol registration. Data and analytic code availability are not addressed in the blinded manuscript—no repository or code DOI is referenced—justifying a low data-availability score; supplementary materials (File S1/S2, Figures S1–S4, Table S1) are referenced but not accessible for this review.

novelty_literature.justification: The research question (adding bevacizumab to chemoimmunotherapy in non-squamous NSCLC) has been directly addressed by IMpower150 (positive OS/PFS) and more recently IMpower151, as well as prior NMAs cited in the manuscript (e.g., Liu et al., ref 32). The real-world cohort provides incremental external validity but is single-center and modest in size. The NMA includes only 4 trials and reproduces previously reported patterns (PFS gain without OS gain and increased toxicity). Methodological novelty is minimal; the authors highlight the RaCE rank-cluster approach as a novel analytic touch, but this is a modest incremental addition. The subgroup observations (PD-L1-negative, elderly, brain metastases) are hypothesis-generating but overlap with existing IMpower150 subgroup analyses.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well organized, with a coherent narrative from question to conclusions. The abstract is quantitatively grounded and consistent with the Results. Methods are appropriately detailed (PSM parameters, caliper, SMD threshold), and the Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings, acknowledges limitations (retrospective design, exploratory subgroup analyses, missing PD-L1 data), and avoids over-claiming given the null OS and increased toxicity. Minor issues: some repetition between Discussion and Conclusions regarding the risk–benefit tradeoff, and figure legends are not visible for independent assessment. Acronyms are generally defined on first use (I+C, I+C+B, PSM, SMD, ORR).

key_strengths: Clinically relevant question with hybrid design (real-world cohort + NMA) and consistent findings across both analyses
Appropriate use of PSM with reported SMD-based balance assessment and caliper of 0.05 SD
Explicit acknowledgment of exploratory nature of subgroup analyses and absence of multiple-testing correction
PRISMA-NMA adherence stated with checklist and risk-of-bias assessment via Cochrane tool
Balanced, cautionary interpretation emphasizing toxicity signal (fatal AE RR 3.51) and lack of OS gain
key_concerns: Low novelty: findings largely reconfirm IMpower150/IMpower151 and prior NMAs without substantive new mechanistic or clinical insight
PSM covariate set omits PD-L1 and performance status; residual confounding likely given selection bias toward I+C+B eligibility (authors concede)
No power calculation and only 80 per arm post-PSM, limiting ability to detect OS differences
NMA includes only 4 trials with fixed-effects pooling and indirect comparisons on sparse network
Data and code availability not addressed in the manuscript body
45.8% PD-L1 missingness limits strength of the key PD-L1-negative subgroup claim
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently executed but incremental real-world + NMA study with a cautionary bottom line. The combination of modest sample, limited PSM covariates, sparse NMA network, and overlap with prior IMpower150 literature places it at a mid-tier general oncology journal (Tier 3) with minor revisions to clarify data availability and strengthen limitations around residual confounding.
